stories.title: Climate change may help eliminate malaria from West and Central Africa
stories.summary: Global warming may make it too hot for malaria-carrying mosquitoes to survive in parts of Africa, but could also shift the problem to less affected areas
stories.extract:
By the end of this century, malaria could be eradicated in West and Central Africa, two of the worst-affected regions. A modelling study suggests cases will plummet in these areas if the extreme heat caused by climate change makes them uninhabitable for mosquitoes. But this also means malaria is expected to become more pronounced in the cooler regions of Africa.
“The overall story is that the burden is shifting,” says Tamma Carleton at the University of California, Berkeley.

stories.summary: A new technique reveals human evolution was rife with interbreeding The post You’re Carrying “Ghost DNA” From Extinct Hominins appeared first on Nautilus .

According to a new study published in Science, all modern humans carry ancient genetic sequences from so-called “ghost ancestors”—lineages of hominins that died out tens and hundreds of thousands of years ago.
